questions.question: With reference to Indian National movement, the famous Safety valve theory is associated with which of the following?
questions.questionHtml: With reference to Indian National movement, the famous Safety valve theory is associated with which of the following?

options.text: Political agendas used by moderate leaders of congress.
options.html: Political agendas used by moderate leaders of congress.

options.text: Methods used by revolutionary activists against British officials.
options.html: Methods used by revolutionary activists against British officials.

options.text: Demand of separate nation by Muslim League.
options.html: Demand of separate nation by Muslim League.

questions.solution: The Safety Valve Theory is linked to the formation of the Indian National Congress. It suggests that A.O. Hume, under guidance from Lord Dufferin, initiated the Congress to provide a peaceful outlet for growing public discontent, preventing violent uprisings.

questions.question: With reference to modern Indian history, who among the following nationalists were the moderates? 1. Aurobindo Ghose 2. Phirozshah Mehta 3. Gopal Krishna Gokhale 4. Lala Lajpat Rai
questions.questionHtml:
With reference to modern Indian history, who among the following nationalists were the moderates?

1. Aurobindo Ghose

2. Phirozshah Mehta

3. Gopal Krishna Gokhale

4. Lala Lajpat Rai
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 2 and 3.

Important Points

  • The leading figures during the first phase of the National Movement (1885-1905) were moderates.

Leading moderates were:

  • A.O. Hume, W.C. Banerjee, Surendra Nath Banerjee, Phirozshah Mehta, Gopalakrishna Gokhale, Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya, Badruddin Tyabji, Justice Ranade, G.Subramanya Aiyar.
  • The closing decade of the nineteenth century and early years of the twentieth century witnessed the emergence of a new and younger group within the Indian National Congress, which was sharply critical of the ideology and the methods of the old leadership.

These extremists were:

  • Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal and Aurobindo Ghose.

questions.question: Which among the following organisation has been founded by Satish Chandra Basu in Bengal?
questions.questionHtml: Which among the following organisation has been founded by Satish Chandra Basu in Bengal?
questions.solution: Satish Chandra Basu founded the Anushilan Samiti in Bengal, a revolutionary organization aimed at promoting nationalist sentiments and preparing youth for armed resistance against British rule. It played a significant role in fostering political awareness and encouraging active participation in the Indian freedom movement.

questions.question: Which of the following was the primary task taken up by the Paramahansa Mandali?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following was the primary task taken up by the Paramahansa Mandali?

options.text: Removal of heavy export duties on Indian goods.
options.html: Removal of heavy export duties on Indian goods.

options.text: Propagate the teachings of the Vedas.
options.html: Propagate the teachings of the Vedas.

questions.solution:
Option 3 is the correct answer.

Important Points

Paramahansa Mandali:

  • It was founded by Dadoba Pandurang and Ramchandra Jaykar in Maharashtra in 1849.
  • Its founders believed in one God and were primarily interested in breaking caste rules. So, option 3 is correct.
  • At its meetings, members took food cooked by low caste people.
  • They also believed in education for women, widow remarriage.

questions.question: Who among the following founded an expatriate Communist Party of India at Tashkent in 1920?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following founded an expatriate Communist Party of India at Tashkent in 1920?
questions.solution: MN Roy founded the expatriate Communist Party of India in Tashkent in 1920. He collaborated with Abani Mukharji and others to establish the party. Roy was a revolutionary and political theorist who later embraced radical humanism, moving away from orthodox Marxism after World War II.

questions.question: Which of the following founders and organizations pair(s) is/are correctly matched? 1. Radhakanta deb: Widow Remarriage Association 2. Keshub Chandra Sen: Tabernacle of New Dispensation 3. Annie Besant: Theosophical society
questions.questionHtml:
Which of the following founders and organizations pair(s) is/are correctly matched?

1. Radhakanta deb: Widow Remarriage Association

2. Keshub Chandra Sen: Tabernacle of New Dispensation

3. Annie Besant: Theosophical society
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 2 only.

 

  • Widow remarriage association was founded by Vishnu Shastri Pandit and M.G.Ranade in 1856. Hence pair 1 is not correctly matched.
  • The Tabernacle of New Dispensation church and the newly constructed chapel foundation was laid by Keshub Chandra Sen in 1869. Hence pair 2 is correctly matched.
    • He introduced the Flag ceremony, the Arati, the Savitri Vrata, the pilgrimage to saints, and other innovations into the church.
    • He said that it is a Divine message to India that comes not to destroy but to fulfill the law and the prophets.
  • Theosophical Society was founded in the USA in 1875 by H.P. Blavatsky and an American Col. H.S. Olcott. Hence pair 3 is not correctly matched.
    • It spread in India under Annie besant in 1893.
    • She was an important person in the Indian freedom struggle.

questions.question: "Poona Sarvajanik Sabha" worked with which of the following ideas?
questions.questionHtml: "Poona Sarvajanik Sabha" worked with which of the following ideas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Sovereign.

Key Points

  • Poona Sarvajanik Sabha was a sociopolitical organization in British India that started with the aim of working as a mediating body between the government and people of India and to popularise the peasants' legal rights.
  • It is formed on April 2, 1870.
  • M. G. Ranade founded the 'Poona Sarvajanik Sabha' in 1870, to represent the Government, the aspiration of the people.
  • Ganesh Vasudeo Joshi was a prominent leader of the Sabha.
    It started as an elected body of 95 members elected by 6000 persons.
  • The organization was a precursor to the Indian National Congress which started with its first session from Maharashtra itself.
  • The first President of the Pune Sarvajanik Sabha was the Shrimant Shrinivasrao Pant Pratinidhi.
  • Rao Bahadur Vizirungum Aya Mudliar was appointed as Chairman of the Managing Committee.
  • Many eminent personalities such as Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Gopal Hari Deshmukh, Maharshi Annasaheb Patwardhan, etc. served as the Presidents of the organization.
  •  In 2016, Meera Pavagi was elected as the first woman President of the organization.

questions.question: Read the following statements on emergence of Nationalism and choose the correct option. A. The Indian National Congress was founded in the year 1885 . B. The early Nationalist leaders were largely from rural and uneducated background.
questions.questionHtml:
Read the following statements on emergence of Nationalism and choose the correct option.

A. The Indian National Congress was founded in the year 1885 .

B. The early Nationalist leaders were largely from rural and uneducated background.

options.text: A is true but B is false
options.html: A is true but B is false

options.text: A is false but B is true
options.html: A is false but B is true

options.text: Both A and B are true
options.html: Both A and B are true

options.text: Both A and B are false
options.html: Both A and B are false

questions.solution:
The correct answer is A is true but B is false.

Key Points

  • The need for an all-India organisation of educated Indians had been felt since 1880, but the Ilbert Bill controversy deepened this desire.
  • The Indian National Congress was established when 72 delegates from all over the country met at Bombay in December 1885. Hence, statement A is true.
  • The early leadership – Dadabhai Naoroji, Pherozeshah Mehta, Badruddin Tyabji, W.C. Bonnerji, Surendranath Banerji, Romesh Chandra Dutt, S. Subramania Iyer, among others – was largely from Bombay and Calcutta.
  • Naoroji, a businessman and publicist settled in London, and for a time member of the British Parliament, guided the younger nationalists. Therefore,  statement B is false.

  • A retired British official, A.O. Hume, also played a part in bringing Indians from the various regions together. 

Therefore, the correct answer is A is true but B is false.

questions.question: Which revolutionary organisation was Barindra Kumar Ghosh a key leader of in Bengal?
questions.questionHtml: Which revolutionary organisation was Barindra Kumar Ghosh a key leader of in Bengal?
questions.solution: Barindra Kumar Ghosh was a key leader of the revolutionary organisation Anushilan Samiti in Bengal. It was a secret society that played a significant role in the Indian independence movement, promoting armed resistance against British colonial rule and fostering patriotic sentiments among the youth.

questions.question: Who among the following moved the first resolution in the first session of the Indian National Congress?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following moved the first resolution in the first session of the Indian National Congress?
questions.solution: G. Subramaniya Iyer moved the first resolution in the first session of the Indian National Congress, held in Bombay in 1885. He was a founding member of INC. The session was presided over by W.C. Banerjee, marking a significant milestone in the history of India's freedom movement.
